podcast.title: Definition and Origins
podcast.body: D-Beat is a derivative of UK Hardcore, named after a distinctive drum pattern central to many of its songs. It emerged from an amalgamation of British punk (like The Sex Pistols) and the New Wave of British Heavy Metal bands from the early 1980s, with Motorhead being a significant influence. "UK Hardcore was an amalgamation of British punk, especially the Sex Bistels, and the new wave of British heavy metal bands that appeared at the beginning of the 1980s."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: UK Hardcore Derivative
podcast.body: D-Beat is a derivative of hardcore that emerged in the UK, characterized by a distinctive drum pattern. It was an amalgamation of British punk and the New Wave of British Heavy Metal, with Motörhead being a major influence. "Then we have the UK, home of a hardcore derivative called Debeat, which referred to a distinctive sort of drum pattern that went with a lot of the songs. UK Hardcore was an amalgamation of British punk, especially the Sex Bistels, and the new wave of British heavy metal bands that appeared at the beginning of the 1980s. The biggest influence from that scene was Motorhead."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
